data.long_meaning: Ida is a form of Goddess Parvati, the consort of Lord Shiva. Idika is the name given to the daughter born to Ida. The name Idika carries the meaning “Daughter of Ida” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Idika usually hope their child will grow to embody daughter of ida and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Idika total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu mythology, Ida is one of the many names of Goddess Parvati, the divine consort of Lord Shiva. She is known to be the embodiment of purity, love, and compassion. In southern India, Idikka or Idambi is one of the numerous names given to the incarnations of Devi or the Mother Goddess. Idika refers to the impression or mark that Idambi leaves upon the hearts of her devotees. It is a reminder of her ever-enduring presence and love. In some parts of Tamil Nadu, the name Idika has been associated with 'Idikkal Amman', a form of the Goddess, known to fulfill the wishes of her devotees.
data.spiritual_significance: Idika holds a significant spiritual significance as it represents the divine blessings and love of Goddess Parvati. It is believed that the name Idika is a source of strength and protection for the devotees. The very sound of the name is said to evoke feelings of purity and peace. Idika embodies the unconditional love, grace, and compassion of the Mother Goddess, who is always seen nurturing and caring for her children. Her name symbolizes hope and the belief that no matter what life's challenges may be, the Divine Mother is always there to provide guidance, support and comfort. Devotees or parents who name their child Idika express their deep love and faith towards the Goddess and seek her blessings for their child's well-being and happiness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Idika is a Sanskrit name derived from the word "Idam" meaning 'this' or 'here' and "Da" meaning 'giver' or 'bestower'. In Hinduism, Idika is believed to represent the divine power that bestows the present moment and the experiences of the material world. It signifies the presence and grace of the divine in everyday life.

historical_references.reference: Idika was a famous Vedic sage, mentioned in the Mahabharata and other ancient Hindu texts. He is believed to have lived during the Vedic period, around 1500-500 BCE.
Idika is also known as the author of the Idika Samhita, a part of the Atharvaveda. This text deals with rituals and mantras for protection from evil spirits and diseases.

modern_usage.modern_context: Idika is a name of reverence in the world of South Indian cuisine, particularly for Idlis. Modern Idika users can be found sharing their Idli making techniques and recipes on Instagram using the hashtag #IdliWorld. On YouTube, Idika is a common search term for learning to make perfect Idlis using traditional methods and modern gadgets like Idli steaming racks. Food bloggers and enthusiasts often use the term Idika to discuss their experiences with the dish, its history, and their personal methods of preparation.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Idika, a teacher in Hyderabad, India, shares that their name Idika meaning "Daughter of Ida" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
